manager_rule: When both absorbed >= 1 AND trimmed_spurs >= 1 occur in the same round AND the post-absorption stub nets list contains zero /SENSEC*_HI or /SENSEC*_LO net names, the halt payload required by Rules 8 and 11 MUST include a component-level attribution step before setting either exclusion-broken flag: (i) log the trimmer's full input stub list (the raw compiler output before any trimming), (ii) log the trimmer's full output stub list (which is the absorber's exact input), and (iii) log the absorber's full output stub list (the final stub set forwarded to FR). If any /SENSEC*_HI or /SENSEC*_LO net name is present in (i) but absent from (ii), set trimmer_exclusion_broken=True and invoke Rule 11's halt protocol for that net. If any /SENSEC*_HI or /SENSEC*_LO net name is present in (ii) but absent from (iii), set absorber_exclusion_broken=True and invoke Rule 8's halt protocol for that net. If /SENSEC* nets are absent from all three lists, both flags must be set and both halt protocols invoked. Human clearance requires separate code diffs and test results for each flagged tool; clearing only one flag while the other remains set does not authorize FR resumption. This attribution requirement is mandatory because a round where both mechanisms ran cannot be remediated by a single targeted fix without knowing which tool performed the purge — applying only the absorber exclusion-list correction when the trimmer also removed Kelvin stubs would leave a live code defect that produces the same outcome on the next dispatch.
